The Standalone Controller & Tools present some new aspects related to licensing as compared to a traditional Ovation system.  In a traditional system, the licensing information is generated and entered on the Database Server.  In a Standalone configuration, however, there is no Database Server.  Because of this, licensing will be done differently.
	A license will be needed for the instance of the tools running on the user’s laptop/PC.
	A license will be needed for the Standalone Controller
	Licensing for the APC toolkit will be associated with the controller
	Licensing for SCADA/CPS protocols will be associated with the controller
	Locking codes for the controller license will be generated based upon the controller MAC address
	The OCC100 point tiers for the OCC100 (OMC100 future) version will be implemented the same as in a Traditional Ovation System.

To not have explicit networking requirements for a controller pair, the standalone controllers will not communicate DDBs (Dynamic Data Blocks) to each other over the network.  All communications will occur over the backplane.  If the controllers communicated over a network, it is possible that DDBs would interfere with each other. [Source Req 1.11]
No changes in the controller code will be required to handle the maximum number of points. This is currently done via a configuration parameter set by Developer’s Studio.
[Source Req. 1.2]

The controller code will handle storing a predefined list of files/folders from the standalone tools.  These files will include things like the database, licensing files, control sheets, graphics, etc.  It will be everything needed to engineer and operate the standalone controller, (except for the software applications themselves). [Source Req 1.3]

When the controller is running in a redundant configuration, it will send the configuration files to the backup controller so that the files are available for runtime use (operator graphics, signal diagrams, etc.) if the primary controller becomes offline.  [Source Req 1.4]
All algorithms will be supported with the exception [Source Req 1.5]:
	SIS algorithms
	Fieldbus algorithms
	Persisval algorithm (this requires a database server)

Algorithm templates/symbols will need to be stored on the controller so that when an algorithm is patched, the corresponding template files will always be “in-sync” with the patched version of the algorithm.  The tool (database and control builder) will need to use the version of the templates/symbols that were from the controller. [Source Req 1.5]
Controller bumpless transfer will perform the same as in a traditional Ovation system.

The controller can support secure communications via a Virtual Private Network (VPN).  The controller will implement a VPN natively in controller and will require a router to terminate the other end of the VPN in the remote location (i.e. Control Room). [Source Req 1.10]

The Standalone Tools will support booting a controller from a blank flash (i.e. from the factory) for the initial configuration, or during a re-format of the flash drive during a field troubleshooting process.

The controller will support the standard SSH connection for advanced\field troubleshooting.  In a standard Ovation system, the SSH authentication is done via RADIUS, however for the Standalone Controller, the authentication will be done via the local user account information stored on the controller.  Only users with the Administrator role will be permitted access.  If no account information is available (no user yet created) SSH access to the controller will be denied.

Step Action: User accounts will be maintained in (and authenticated by) the Standalone Controller.  As it relates specifically to the Standalone Controller, there will be 3 different “User Types” to which a user may be assigned:

	Operator:  The user will not be able to perform any engineering functions.  All Engineering Tools applications will consider the database to be in a read-only mode.  (Reference Section 14.2.5.3 for more information about read-only mode in Ovation Developer Studio.)
	Engineer:  The user will be able to perform engineering functions and make modifications to the database.
	Administrator:  The user will be able to perform engineering functions and make modifications to the database, user accounts, and Ovation security configurations.

These user accounts will be used for the purpose of connecting and gaining access to a Standalone Controller’s runtime and engineering/configuration data.  They will not be associated in any way with the computer’s Windows user.  [Source Req. 2.7]

The Ovation Security Manager (launched from Ovation Developer Studio) will be responsible for creating and maintaining users in the Standalone Controller and defining allow/deny access to Ovation functionality for those users.  Although the Ovation Security Manager will provide the user interface to create/modify/delete user accounts and update/reset existing user passwords, the underlying functionality for these operations will be performed by the Standalone Controller itself.  [Source Req. 1.12] [Source Req. 2.10]

Step Action: To connect to a Standalone Controller, the user will need to provide a valid username and password – authenticated by the Standalone Controller.  The tools for Standalone Controller software will support the following example use cases when connecting to a Standalone Controller:

If the user is defined with the role of Operator, they will still be able to run Ovation Developer Studio (subject to the user’s Ovation security configuration), but the application will execute in read-only mode.  (Reference Section 14.2.5.3 for more information about read-only mode in Ovation Developer Studio.)
	Initial configuration of a Standalone Controller (e.g., no database currently exists in the Standalone Controller).
	Off-line configuration of a new database (e.g., new control scheme/functionality) – completely replacing the database on (and the application currently running in) the Standalone Controller.

	Off-line modification of a Standalone Controller.  For example, the user Disconnects from the Standalone Controller but keeps the database locally on the computer to make “off-line” engineering modifications to the database.  (Reference Section 14.2.4 for more information about Disconnect.)
Note that this use case will not be applicable for users defined with the role of Operator.

Checks will be performed to verify that the database running locally on the computer is compatible with the database currently stored in the Standalone Controller.  If an incompatibility is detected, the user will be notified and given the following options:
	Abort the Connection attempt.
	Utilize the database on the Standalone Controller – in which case the database currently on the computer will be deleted and the database will be uploaded from the Standalone Controller.

	Utilize the database currently on the computer.  Note that since the database has been detected to be incompatible with the database stored on (and application running in) the Standalone Controller, the Standalone Controller will need to be cleared.
Once Connected to the Standalone Controller, the Ovation HMI and utility applications can be executed, regardless of the user’s defined role.  [Source Req. 3.1]

Unless the user is defined with the role of Operator, the Standalone Controller will implicitly mark its database as locked (or “signed out”). [Source Req. 2.11] However, only one user will have the ability to Connect and lock a Standalone Controller’s database at any one time.  If a non-Operator user attempts to Connect to a Standalone Controller whose database is already locked, they will be notified and given the following options:
	Abort the Connection attempt.
	Continue with the Connection, but without locking the database and operating in read-only mode.
	Override the database lock.

In the case of a redundant Standalone Controller, Connection for engineering purpose will require the availability of (and explicit connection to) the primary half of the redundant Standalone Controller.  If the primary half is not available, the user will still be able to perform a Connect for the purposes of operator functionality (including access to the database in a read-only mode).  (Reference Section 14.2.5.3 for more information about read-only mode in Ovation Developer Studio.)

Note, if the primary controller is lost, and a database backup is not available offline, the user can still recover the database from the backup controller and use that as a starting point to recover the primary controller.  Best practice should be for the user to always archive the database in another location following any engineering changes to the application.

Step Action: The Disconnect operation will close the connection with the Standalone Controller.  All HMI applications will be terminated, and the user will be logged out of the Standalone Controller.  In addition, if the Standalone Controller database is not locked (e.g., Operator user), the database on the workstation will be deleted/removed.  If the Standalone Controller database is locked, the tools for software will support several options when disconnecting [Source Req. 2.12]:

	Disconnect (Normal):  The Standalone Controller database (and supporting files) will be downloaded to the Standalone Controller, the Standalone Controller will indicate that its database is no longer locked, and the database on the workstation will be deleted/removed.  This will be the typical use case.

	Disconnect (Engineer):  The Standalone Controller database (and supporting files) will be downloaded to the Standalone Controller and the Standalone Controller will indicate that its database is still locked by the user, and the database on the workstation will not be deleted/removed.
This use case is appropriate if additional engineering functions are intended to be performed in an offline (or disconnected) state.

The Standalone HMI Applications can be initiated after the user is connected to the Standalone Controller.  When the user connects as an Operator, the data that the HMI Applications use, such as configuration, data files, etc., will be uploaded and installed. [Source Req 3.1]
A user can only connect to one controller at a time from a specific computer.  [Source Req 3.2]

Multiple users (operators, engineers, or administrators) will be able to connect to the same Standalone Controller providing they connect from different machines. The Standalone Controller will allow at least three simultaneous connections. [Source Req 3.3] Once the user is connected, they will be able to initiate the HMI Applications. When the user disconnects from the Standalone Controller, any running HMI Applications will terminate.
The following HMI Applications will be supported in the Standalone Mode. [Source Req 3.4]
	Graphics
	Point Information
	Trend
	Point Review
	Standalone Alarm Window
	Signal Diagram
	Ovation Machine Works
	Sensor Calibrate
	Controller Diagnostics
	Session Manager
	Error Log

The Standalone HMI Alarm Software will only provide the current points in alarm.  This supports only an “Alarm List” none of the other “List” types are available. The Standalone HMI Software will not provide the following:
	Alarm Printer
	Audible Alarm
	Alarm Graphics Groups (However the priority icon will be supported)
	Alert Details (Fieldbus is not being supported)
	Ovation Keyboard

The Standalone HMI Applications will support the Ovation Security Rules, which enables or disables the ability to perform the Operator Functions (such as scan on, scan off, etc.) based on the user that is currently logged into the Standalone Controller.
